_doc: Cele mai bune orașe din lume pentru o viață de calitate. Note de judecată pe baza indicelui EIU de calitate a vieții 2026 (primele 10 orașe și Auckland, pe 12) și, pentru celelalte poziții, a clasamentelor Mercer 2024, Happy City Index 2026 și Monocle 2025.

items.name: Copenhaga
items.why: Primul oraș din lume în indicele EIU 2026 (98 de puncte), pentru al doilea an la rând, cu note maxime la stabilitate, educație și infrastructură; locuințele sunt scumpe.
items.whyEn: The world’s first city in the 2026 EIU index (98 points), for the second year running, with top marks for stability, education and infrastructure; housing is expensive.

items.name: Viena

items.whyEn: Second in the world (97 points), with its best marks in healthcare, education and infrastructure. Social housing makes rents more affordable than in other rich capitals.

items.name: Melbourne

items.whyEn: Third in the world (97 points), with 100 in healthcare and education and 96 in culture and environment. Housing is expensive relative to income, and heatwaves and bushfires are a risk.

items.name: Sydney

items.whyEn: Fourth in the world (97 points), up from 6th. Spectacular nature and many jobs, but one of the world’s most expensive housing markets relative to income.

items.whyEn: Fifth in the world (96 points), down from joint 2nd, because of lower marks in culture and environment. Very high wages, but extremely expensive housing.

items.name: Osaka

items.whyEn: Seventh in the world (96 points), one of the safest big cities. Housing is much more affordable than in Western Europe or Australia; but the earthquake risk is high.

items.whyEn: Eighth in the world (96 points), the third Australian city in the top 10. Quieter and cheaper than Sydney or Melbourne, but with fewer jobs.

items.whyEn: Ninth in the world (96 points), up one place, the only North American city in the top 10. Exceptional nature, but housing among the most expensive in the world relative to income, and seismic risk.

items.whyEn: Tenth in the world (96 points), rising. The biggest labour market on the list, very safe and very well connected, but crowded and exposed to earthquakes.

items.name: Auckland
items.why: Locul 12 în lume, după ce a coborât cinci locuri și a ieșit din primele 10, cu note mai mici la sănătate și infrastructură. Natură excelentă, dar locuințe scumpe și oraș îndepărtat.
items.whyEn: Twelfth in the world, after falling five places and dropping out of the top 10, with lower marks in healthcare and infrastructure. Excellent nature, but expensive housing and a remote city.

items.name: Helsinki
items.why: Locul 2 în Happy City Index 2026; educație de vârf, servicii publice foarte bune și natură aproape. Iernile sunt lungi și întunecate, iar economia finlandeză crește lent.
items.whyEn: Second in the Happy City Index 2026; top education, very good public services and nature close by. Winters are long and dark, and the Finnish economy is growing slowly.

items.name: München
items.why: Locul 11 la Mercer și 9 în Happy City Index 2026; salarii mari, industrie puternică și Alpii aproape. Cel mai scump oraș din Germania pentru locuințe.
items.whyEn: Eleventh at Mercer and 9th in the Happy City Index 2026; high wages, strong industry and the Alps nearby. Germany’s most expensive city for housing.

items.whyEn: Sixth at Mercer; very international, with a large airport and many company headquarters. Its housing crisis is one of the worst in Europe.

items.why: Locul 18 la Mercer; oraș pe ape, cu un ecosistem tehnologic puternic. Cozile la chirii de lungă durată sunt de ani de zile, iar criminalitatea violentă a crescut.
items.whyEn: Eighteenth at Mercer; a city on the water with a strong tech ecosystem. Waits for long-term rentals last years, and violent crime has risen.

items.whyEn: Twenty-second at Mercer and 14th in the Happy City Index 2026; very high wages, nature at the edge of the city and a rich country. The cost of living is among the highest in the world.

items.whyEn: Thirteenth at Mercer; Canada’s largest city, very diverse, with finance and technology. Housing is very expensive relative to income.

items.why: Locul 22 în Happy City Index 2026; cel mai sigur și mai bine conectat oraș din Asia, cu salarii mari și servicii publice excelente. Locuințele private și mașinile sunt foarte scumpe.
items.whyEn: Twenty-second in the Happy City Index 2026; Asia’s safest and best-connected city, with high wages and excellent public services. Private housing and cars are very expensive.

items.name: Haga
items.why: Locul 14 la Mercer și 15 în Happy City Index 2026; oraș al instituțiilor internaționale, lângă mare, mai liniștit și mai ieftin decât Amsterdam.
items.whyEn: Fourteenth at Mercer and 15th in the Happy City Index 2026; a city of international institutions, by the sea, quieter and cheaper than Amsterdam.

items.name: Wellington
items.why: Locul 14 la Mercer; capitală mică și prietenoasă, cu natură excelentă. Economia Noii Zeelande e slabă, iar riscul de cutremur e ridicat.
items.whyEn: Fourteenth at Mercer; a small, friendly capital with excellent nature. New Zealand’s economy is weak and earthquake risk is high.

items.name: Paris
items.why: Primul loc în clasamentul Monocle 2025; cea mai bogată ofertă culturală din lume și cel mai bun transport din Europa. Locuințele mici și scumpe, aglomerația și siguranța sunt minusurile.
items.whyEn: First in Monocle’s 2025 ranking; the richest cultural offer in the world and the best transport in Europe. Small, expensive homes, crowding and safety are the downsides.
